CITY  OF  ALHAMBRA
  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL

  (Notice No. N2M21-125)

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the regular meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be held
on Monday, October 11, 2021, commencing at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California pursuant to the order of the
Mayor of the City of Alhambra, the Alhambra City Charter, the Alhambra Municipal Code, and
Sections 54955 and 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

Consistent with AB 361, the Alhambra City Council meeting will not be physically open to
the public, although the public may participate by video conference or teleconference and
some of the Council Members may choose to participate via video conference or
teleconference rather than attend in person.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and made
a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

Dated:  October 7, 2021
Notice No.  N2M21-125

muted so that the meeting can proceed.

For those wishing to speak on an agenda or non-agendized item, you have 3 options for participation:
1) Pre-register to speak: Please email Van Nguyen at vnguyen@cityofalhambra.org by 5:00 p.m.
prior to the meeting with the item number you wish to speak on and the phone number you will
use when calling or the name you will use when logging into the meeting. You should then call
or log into the meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will unmute you and announce
you when it is your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless that time is adjusted by
the Mayor. If you do not have access to a computer, please call 626-570-3248 to request public
comment.

2) “Raise your hand”: For those members of the public that wish to speak but did not make a request
via email as described above, such members of the public may speak by using the “Raise Hand”
function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom. Staff will unmute you and announce you
when it is your time to speak. If participating via telephone, the Mayor will ask anyone participating by
telephone if they would like to speak after asking those on Zoom. Staff will unmute telephone callers
and you may state you wish to speak.

you can email your comments to the City Clerk at lmyles@cityofalhambra.org by no later than 5:00
p.m. on October 11, 2021 to ensure that the City Clerk has time to print the emails prior to the
beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record by the City Clerk, with a

comment is received after 5:00 p.m. but before the conclusion of the meeting based upon its time
stamp, the comment will still be included as a part of the record of the meeting but will not be read into

Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated
should email or call the City Clerk at lmyles@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-5090 who will use their

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-125

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the regular meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor in accordance with Section 54955 and
54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES
Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council
taking action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may
determine that the title has been read.

Recommended Action:  By motion, determine that the titles to all ordinances which appear
on this public agenda have been read, and waive further reading.

PRESENTATION

1.  SHORT TERM RENTAL (STR) UPDATE – F2M18-35

  Staff will present to the City Council brief overview and update on Short Term Rentals
  (STRs) in the City including, but not limited to, the number of and types of STRs,
  rates/revenues related to STRs and public safety aspects.

  Recommended Action:  City Council receive and order filed this informational
  report and provide direction to staff as deemed appropriate.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 2 – 10)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda are considered by the City Council to be routine and
will be enacted by one motion unless a citizen or Council member requests otherwise; in which
case, the item will be removed for separate consideration.

 2.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF TWO COMPRESSED NATURAL GAS FUELED
  PASSENGER BUSES FOR ALHAMBRA COMMUNITY TRANSIT – F2M21-6A, C2M21-
  54, M2M21-133

  The 2021-2022 fiscal year budget includes the replacement of two Alhambra CNG
  Community Transit buses. The buses being replaced are 2010 models that have reached
  the end of their useful life of 12 years as allowed by the Federal Transit Administration.
  These older buses have become less reliable resulting in increased maintenance cost and
  occasional disruption of service to the community. Staff is seeking approval to enter into
  a cooperative purchase agreement with Creative Bus Sales to finalize the purchase.
  Cooperative purchase is allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080 section (b)(3).

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to Creative Bus Sales in an amount not
  to exceed $1,160,375.46 for the purchase of two (2) 29-passenger compressed natural
  gas (CNG) buses; and, direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M21-133)

3.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  MAIN STREET, FOURTH STREET, AND MISSION ROAD SEWER MAIN
  REPLACEMENT PROJECT – F2M21-58, RFP2M21-17, C2M21-55, M2M21-134

  On August 9, 2021, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for Professional Engineering Design for the Main Street, 4th Street, and Mission Road
  Sewer Main Replacement Project. The Sewer Master Plan identified Main Street (from
  Atlantic to 4th Street), 4th Street (from Main Street to Mission Road), and Mission Road
  (from 4th Street to Garfield Avenue) as deficient in capacity. As part of the City of
  Alhambra’s continuing efforts to improve the sewer infrastructure this contract will provide
  engineering design, plans, and preparation of bid specifications for the replacement of
  approximately 5,000 feet of existing 8-inch to 12-inch sewer main with a larger capacity
  sewer main. Staff reviewed a total of seven proposals. Hunsaker & Associates Irvine Inc.
  was selected based on distinguished qualifications, experience, reputation,
  responsiveness, availability, and cost.

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  Hunsaker & Associates Irvine Inc. for engineering design services for the Main Street,
  Fourth Street, and Mission Road Sewer Main Replacement Project in an amount not to
  exceed $178,650.00, direct the Finance Director to appropriate funds from the Sewer
  Fund Balance in the amount of $178,650.00 and allocate funding to this project; and, direct
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-134)

4.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  MISSION ROAD SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT BETWEEN MARENGO
  AVENUE AND MARGUERITA AVENUE – F2M21-57, RFP2M21-16, C2M21-56, M2M21-
  135

  4
10-11-21
   On August 9, 2021, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for professional engineering design services for the Mission Road Sewer Main
  Replacement Project. The Sewer Master Plan identified the Mission Road sewer main
  between Marengo Avenue and Marguerita Avenue as deficient in capacity. The Master
  Plan recommends replacement of the existing sewer main with a larger diameter sewer
  main. Staff reviewed a total of seven proposals. West and Associates Engineering, Inc.
  was selected based on their distinguished qualifications, experience, reputation,
  responsiveness, availability, and cost.

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and

  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-135)

5.  AWARD CONTRACT: GRAND AVE., ETHEL AVE., AND CAMPBELL AVE. STREET
  IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT – F2M21-55, N2M21-92, C2M21-57, M2M21-136

  On July 12, 2021, the City Council authorized a Notice Inviting Bids for the Grand Ave.,
  Ethel Ave., and Campbell Ave. Street Improvements Project. On Thursday, September
  16, 2021 the City Clerk received 8 bids that ranged from $333,333.33 to $560,352.03. The
  lowest bid was submitted by All American Asphalt in the amount of $333,333.33. Staff
  reviewed the bid and found it to be in full compliance and conformance with the project
  specifications. All American Asphalt has the necessary licenses to complete the work and
  has conducted similar projects for the City of Alhambra.

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to All American Asphalt in the amount of
  $333,333.33 for the Grand Avenue, Ethel Avenue and Campbell Avenue Improvement
  Project; and, direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M21-136)

6.  ACCEPT GRANT: OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY – SELECTIVE TRAFFIC
  ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM – F2M21-18, F2M1-77, M2M21-137

  Staff requests that the City Council authorize staff to accept the Office of Traffic Safety
  grant in the amount of $127,000. The goal of the Office of Traffic Safety is to reduce the
  number of persons killed or injured in crashes involving alcohol or other primary collision
  factors through grant funding for local law enforcement agencies. The Alhambra Police
  Department intends to utilize the funding for the FY 2021-2022 Selective Traffic
  Enforcement Program to enhance community safety through various enforcement and
  education programs. Such programs and services will include: DUI enforcement,
  awareness and education programs; DUI checkpoints; bicycle and pedestrian safety
  enforcement and education; participation in programs such as National Walk to School
  Day, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Winter & Summer Mobilizations,
  National Bicycle Safety Month, National Teen Driver Safety Week, National Distracted
  Driving Awareness Month, National Motorcycle Safety Month, National Child Passenger

   Safety Week, and California’s Pedestrian Safety Month.

  Recommended Action:  City Council authorize staff to accept the State of California
  Office of Traffic Safety grant in the amount of $127,000; authorize the Chief of Police to
  enter into a contract with the Office of Traffic Safety for the grant; and, direct staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-137)

10.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCES RESTRUCTURING VARIOUS
  BOARDS & COMMISSIONS AND ESTABLISHING THE HUMAN RELATIONS
  COMMISSION AS WELL AS THE HISTORIC PRESERVATION COMMISSION – F2M21-
  36, O2M21-4791, O2M21-4792, O2M21-4793

  From February through June 2021, in response to objectives identified in the City’s 2020-
  2021 Strategic Plan, the City Council discussed a variety of changes to the City’s current
  groups including the installation of new Boards and Commissions. Throughout the
  discussions, the Council focused on changes that will further support the Council and the
  needs of the community and enhance public participation. Staff is requesting that the City
  Council consider second reading and adoption of three ordinances restructuring changes
  to the City’s Boards and Commissions, including the establishment of new Commissions
  – the Human Relations Commission and the Historic Preservation Commission.

1.  SHORT TERM RENTAL (STR) UPDATE – F2M18-35

  Director of Community Development HO presented to the City Council brief overview and

  1
10-11-21
   update on Short Term Rentals (STRs) in the City including, but not limited to, the number
  of and types of STRs, rates/revenues related to STRs and public safety aspects. The
  PowerPoint presentation is available in the City Clerk’s office.

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ referred to concerns received regarding
  problematic STRs such as housing units used for STRs and not as affordable housing for
  families in the Alhambra Unified School District. She suggested charging a Transient
  Occupancy Tax (TOT) on existing STRs, registering new applicants for STRS, and to not
  allow affordable housing to be used as STRs.

  Councilmember MAZA agreed with Ms. Pérez’s suggestions and supported a more formal
  registry as well as business license program for STRs with renewals contingent upon
  review of any complaint records.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER supported future discussion of the suggested
  regulations. She supported a business tax first rather than a TOT to allow for more public
  input. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. HO discussed the history and trends of
  complaints against STRs. They also discussed the effect of STRs on affordable housing
  stock.

  Councilmember MALONEY discussed the differences between a business tax and a
  general tax with City Attorney MONTES as well as the processes for amending any
  existing ordinances. Mr. MALONEY stated that in the short term, he supported
  enforcement of business tax and collection of robust fees for staff work in monitoring
  STRs. He echoed his fellow Concilmember’s concerns regarding the potential negative
  effect of STRs on affordable housing stock in the City. He further discussed enforcement
  and regulation for STRs with Mr. HO and Mr. MONTES. They also discussed a potential
  licensing system, which Mr. Maloney supported.

  Mayor LEE echoed previous concerns regarding STRs and also discussed the TOT tax
  with Mr. HO. Council continued to discuss and provided direction to staff to return with a
  survey of other local cities’ STR monitoring and registration programs after which Council
  would discuss moving forward with regulation.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report and
  directed staff to return with a survey of other local cities’ STR monitoring and registration
  programs.

 6.  ACCEPT GRANT: OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY – SELECTIVE TRAFFIC
  ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM – F2M21-18, F2M1-77, M2M21-137

  Staff requested that the City Council authorize staff to accept the Office of Traffic Safety
  grant in the amount of $127,000. The goal of the Office of Traffic Safety is to reduce the
  number of persons killed or injured in crashes involving alcohol or other primary collision
  factors through grant funding for local law enforcement agencies. The Alhambra Police
  Department intended to utilize the funding for the FY 2021-2022 Selective Traffic
  Enforcement Program to enhance community safety through various enforcement and
  education programs. Such programs and services would include: DUI enforcement,
  awareness and education programs; DUI checkpoints; bicycle and pedestrian safety
  enforcement and education; participation in programs such as National Walk to School
  Day, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Winter & Summer Mobilizations,
  National Bicycle Safety Month, National Teen Driver Safety Week, National Distracted
  Driving Awareness Month, National Motorcycle Safety Month, National Child Passenger
  Safety Week, and California’s Pedestrian Safety Month.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to accept the State of California Office of
  Traffic Safety grant in the amount of $127,000; authorized the Chief of Police to enter into
  a contract with the Office of Traffic Safety for the grant; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-137)
